page: Microsoft Azure FX8-4ms_v2 is a specialized virtual machine configuration engineered for environments that require elevated clock speeds combined with an expansive memory footprint. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture operating at 4.2 GHz. The compute topology provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is substantial at 168 GB of RAM, offering 42 GB of memory per vCPU alongside 260 MB of L3 cache. The CPU incorporates advanced vector and matrix instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX extensions. Local storage is not included, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage.

Benchmark results reflect the instance's high-frequency, low-core-count profile. Geekbench single-core performance ranks in the top ten percent, achieving a score of 2351.0, paired with strong single-threaded throughput in compression and decompression routines. Multi-threaded benchmark results, such as Clang compilation and multi-core stress testing, fall into lower percentiles due to the four-vCPU hardware limit. Memory subsystem testing shows cached small-block read speeds reaching 345.37 GB/s, though large-block uncached read and write bandwidth drop to 36.1 GB/s and 25.44 GB/s respectively. Redis SET throughput measures at 6.27 million operations per second, indicating steady performance in transactional memory tasks.

The qualitative efficiency profile of the FX8-4ms_v2 is driven by its high memory-to-core ratio. By allocating 168 GB across only four vCPUs, it minimizes compute resource overhead for software systems constrained by per-core commercial licensing models. The instance is suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caches, electronic design automation (EDA), and financial modeling applications where single-thread performance and memory headroom are primary requirements.
